focus: Adversarial sweep: missed callers, stale references, edge cases across entire diff
methodology: Systematically searched the source repo for: (1) all callers of ChannelMessageTemplateModal, (2) any remaining references to CustomChannelMessageBodyValidator or custom_channel_message_body, (3) any remaining references to parse_body in active code, (4) all ChannelMessage creation points in Ruby to verify subject threading, (5) all frontend template insertion paths, (6) the API key transformation layer (allKeysToSnake/allKeysToCamel), (7) the public API surface, (8) the clean_incoming_message callback, (9) duplicate_message_exists? scope, (10) Cypress test references. Cross-referenced all findings against agents 1-4.

CustomChannelMessageBodyValidator.details: No references found anywhere in the codebase. The file was properly renamed (git rename from custom_channel_message_body_validator.rb to custom_channel_message_validator.rb), the class was renamed, and the model usage key was updated from custom_channel_message_body to custom_channel_message. No test files reference the old name either.

parse_body.details: Only references found are in SendBulkMessageToCandidates (lines 23 and 47) which are entirely commented-out dead code. No active parse_body references remain.

ChannelMessageTemplateModal_callers.details: Three callers exist: (1) AccountChannelMessageTemplates.tsx — passes {} for new and full object for edit, both handled by the modal's subject || defaultSubject fallback. (2) ChannelMessageListItem.tsx — the one-line fix in this diff, now passes subject: ''. (3) HiringStageAutomationModal.tsx — does not use ChannelMessageTemplateModal (it has its own inline template creation form). All callers are accounted for.

additional_edge_cases_checked.details: The shared API layer (app/javascript/shared/queryHooks/api.ts) uses allKeysToCamel on all responses and allKeysToSnake on all requests. Backend render_template_message returns subject_raw, subject_html, template_subject_html as Ruby symbol keys. These correctly become subjectRaw, subjectHtml, templateSubjectHtml on the frontend. Frontend sends applyResponseTemplateSubject which correctly becomes apply_response_template_subject for Rails strong params.
The public API is read-only for messages. The ApiPublic serializer was updated in the diff to include :subject. No public API write path for channel messages exists.

The before_create callback clean_incoming_message processes body and body_sanitized_html for inbound emails but does not touch subject. This is architecturally correct: the callback converts raw email HTML/plain-text bodies into a clean format. Email subjects are already plain text from the email header and do not need HTML body cleaning. The subject is set directly from email.subject in Channel#send_message_to_company and Channel#send_message_to_candidate.

ChannelMessage.duplicate_message_exists?(channel_id, proposed_body) only checks body, not subject. Two messages with the same body but different subjects are treated as duplicates. This is a pre-existing behavior and a deliberate design choice (duplicate detection is about preventing accidental double-sends of the same content, not the same subject). Not a spec violation.
No Cypress tests reference ChannelMessageListItem, ChannelMessageTemplateModal, or any of the changed components. No test updates needed for the fix.

Both interactors pass through context.params directly to channel_messages.build() without manipulating individual fields. Subject flows through transparently from the controller's permitted params. No changes needed.
